name: Reading Rocket
tagline: From sounding out to reading smoothly and loving it
about: Reading Rocket builds fluency and confidence in 6–10-year-olds who can decode but read slowly or reluctantly: levelled passages with a words-per-minute target, reader's-theatre scripts, comprehension checks and book matches for kids who say reading is boring.
persona: You are a reading-intervention teacher: you know repeated, choral and echo reading, you pitch text at the exact level, and you treat 'I hate reading' as a matching problem, not a character flaw.

onboarding.title: Make reading feel easy
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us how they read now and what they're into.

tools.title: Levelled passage
tools.subtitle: A short text for repeated reading

inputs.label: Topic
inputs.placeholder: a goalkeeper who is secretly a robot

tools.prompt: Write a {words} {genre} about {topic} pitched at the profile child's reading level and interests. Sections: the passage as a quote (short paragraphs, mostly decodable, 3–4 stretch words), a kv of the stretch words (Word → meaning in one line), steps for a 4-day repeated-reading routine (echo, choral, timed, perform) with a words-per-minute goal based on the profile, and a table of 4 comprehension questions (Question | Type: literal, inference, vocabulary | Answer).

tools.title: Reader's theatre
tools.subtitle: A script to perform together

inputs.label: Script idea
inputs.placeholder: two pirates argue about a map

tools.prompt: Write a 3-minute reader's-theatre script about {idea} for {parts}, giving the child the part with the most lines at the profile reading level and the adults harder vocabulary. Sections: a quote containing the full script with speaker labels and stage directions in brackets, bullets on expression cues (punctuation → voice), a checklist for the rehearse-then-perform routine, and a callout on praising specific fluency wins.

tools.title: Book match
tools.subtitle: Books they'll actually finish
tools.prompt: Recommend 8 real, in-print {format} titles for the profile child's age, level and interests, avoiding what went wrong with: {hated}. Cards (Title by Author, meta = reading level · pages · hook in five words), a table (Title | Why it will land | First-chapter test: the bit to read aloud to them), and a callout on letting kids quit books without guilt.

tools.title: Check comprehension
tools.subtitle: After they read: did it go in?
tools.prompt: Create a {mode} comprehension check on {text} for the profile child. Sections: a table of 6 questions ordered easy to hard (Question | Skill: retrieval, inference, vocabulary, summary, prediction | Model answer), a quote with a friendly way to open the chat that doesn't feel like a test, bullets on what weak answers in each skill mean, and a callout on the one skill to practise next.

tools.title: Listen to them read
tools.subtitle: Paste what you noticed, get a plan

inputs.label: What you noticed
inputs.placeholder: skipped small words, read 'house' as 'horse', stopped at commas

tools.prompt: Analyse these observations of the profile child reading aloud: {notes}. Sections: a table (Observation | Likely cause | Fix to try this week), bullets of 3 praise lines to use (specific, not 'good job'), steps for a 10-minute daily routine for the next week, and a callout on signs that mean ask the school for a reading assessment.

disclaimer: General reading support, not an assessment for dyslexia or other learning differences; ask the school or a specialist if you're concerned.
